# AtomSched best-kernel structure checklist

Reference: `rsi-round19-clean`, kernel `s3b_sep_g16_pers132_w1`.

## Optimisations 1–9

| # | Structural decision | Authored HIR | Finalized TIR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 128×256×64 CTA tile; producer warp plus two consumer warpgroups; 64×256×16 SS WGMMA repeated `(2, 1, 4)`; A K-major SW128 and B MN-major SW128 | `hir/gemm_8192x17408x5120_optimal.py:18-21`, `:27-37`, `:52-57`, `:66-87` | `tir/gemm_8192x17408x5120_optimal.py:32-34`, `:50-82`, `:83-121`, `:127-268`, `:270-426` |
| 2 | The earlier four-stage TMA ring established staged loading; the winning kernel supersedes its depth with item 9's three stages | `hir/gemm_8192x17408x5120_optimal.py:20-21`, `:69-80` | `tir/gemm_8192x17408x5120_optimal.py:57-82`, `:83-110` |
| 3 | Spread the tile traversal over 132 persistent CTAs | `hir/gemm_8192x17408x5120_optimal.py:22`, `:40-43`, `:51`, `:60-63` | `tir/gemm_8192x17408x5120_optimal.py:14`, `:35-48` |
| 4 | `wait_group 1` is an asynchronous WGMMA synchronization depth, so it remains a CUDA instruction-selection detail | `hir/gemm_8192x17408x5120_optimal.py:82-87` states the synchronous MMA | `tir/gemm_8192x17408x5120_optimal.py:153-268`, `:311-426` states the same synchronous MMA operations |
| 5 | N-major order with M tiles inside it, retained inside each group | `hir/gemm_8192x17408x5120_optimal.py:60-65` (`bn` encloses `mi`) | `tir/gemm_8192x17408x5120_optimal.py:35-48`; A and B windows are `:85-100` |
| 6 | Convert the accumulator to bf16, copy it to an N-contiguous SW128 shared tile, and TMA-store that tile | `hir/gemm_8192x17408x5120_optimal.py:34`, `:89-97` | `tir/gemm_8192x17408x5120_optimal.py:37-47`, `:428-461` |
| 7 | The BK32/six-stage experiment introduced C staging outside the load ring; the winner retains separate C staging while item 9 supersedes BK and depth | `hir/gemm_8192x17408x5120_optimal.py:20-21`, `:89-96` | ring `[0,147456)` at `tir/gemm_8192x17408x5120_optimal.py:57-82`; C staging `[147456,212992)` at `:37-47`, consumed at `:428-461` |
| 8 | Group 16 M tiles while preserving N-major traversal within a group | `hir/gemm_8192x17408x5120_optimal.py:25`, `:60-65` | `tir/gemm_8192x17408x5120_optimal.py:35-48`; windows use `(g * 16 + mi) * 128` and `bn * 256` at `:85-100`, `:456-461` |
| 9 | Winning composition: BK64, three TMA stages, G=16, persistent 132-CTA traversal, and C staging after all six A/B ring slots | `hir/gemm_8192x17408x5120_optimal.py:20-25`, `:40-43`, `:60-96` | `tir/gemm_8192x17408x5120_optimal.py:14`, `:35-110`, `:428-461`; the disjoint intervals are item 7 |

## Added only when translating TIR to CUDA

| CUDA detail | Why it remains outside HIR/TIR |
|---|---|
| TMA tensor-map encoding, including dimensions, strides, boxes, swizzle enum, and L2 promotion | The tensor layouts and windows are stated above; encoding them as `CUtensorMap` objects is instruction lowering. |
| Full/empty mbarriers, expected byte counts, phase parity, and the producer/store completion protocol | The IR instructions are synchronous; asynchronous producer/consumer synchronization is not an authored schedule operation. |
| WGMMA fence, commit, `wait_group 1`, and compiler register fences | These select and order asynchronous PTX instructions for each synchronous `T.tiled_mma`. |
| Shared-memory descriptors with LBO, SBO, base offsets, and hardware swizzle codes | The TIR views state the layouts; descriptor bit encoding belongs to WGMMA lowering. |
| `setmaxnreg 40/232` | Register redistribution is a launch/instruction-level control absent from the schedule IR. |
| `fence.proxy.async.shared::cta` and the barrier before each TMA store | These make generic-proxy shared writes visible to the async-copy proxy; the TIR states a synchronous copy followed by a store. |
| Decomposing the logical 128×256 TMA store into one 64-row bulk instruction issued by each consumer warpgroup | The HIR/TIR states the complete output tile and its one logical copy; instruction partitioning and issuing lanes are CUDA lowering choices. |
| 1024-byte dynamic-shared-memory base alignment | This is an ABI/allocation-base requirement used while encoding TMA and WGMMA addresses. |
| Accumulator-to-PTX-fragment register mapping and packed bf16 conversion | The shard layout and cast state value ownership; physical PTX register order and packing are code generation. |
| Running stage phase/counter bookkeeping across tiles | The TIR states slot `(k // 64) % 3`; carrying asynchronous phase state between tiles is synchronization lowering. |
